title: Guards are given as the reason almost no construct is must; the guard-only run contradicts this
evidence: The abstract says almost no construct is deterministic 'because the extractor does not evaluate the guards almost every such transition passes'. generated-guard-only.tex gives GuardOnlyMust=191, GuardOnlyUnguarded=150 and GuardOnlyGuarded=41, so 150 of the 191 guard-free must edges (78.5%) run no guard at all. results-must/guard-only.json counts 0 guarded edges in realworld and mifos and 3 of 128 in k8sdash. If every guard is taken to pass, the constructs that earn must rise only from CensusMustSites=25 to GuardOnlySites=66, which is 66 of RoundTwoInScope=1777 (3.7%), still 'almost no'.
consequence: The headline explanation for RQ1 points at the wrong cause. Guards account for 41 edges. The scarcity comes from the condition, self-loop and target demotions. ch7 'which is little, rather than what the applications do' and ch5 'where an application puts its guard decides how much' repeat the misattribution.
fix: Abstract: '...once the demotion rules are applied; even taking every guard to let the navigation through raises the tier only from \CensusMust{} to \GuardOnlyMust{} edges and from \CensusMustSites{} to \GuardOnlySites{} constructs.' Delete 'because the extractor does not evaluate the guards almost every such transition passes'. In ch7:25 drop 'rather than what the applications do'. In ch5:1104-1105 replace 'decides how much' with 'moves \GuardOnlyGuarded{} edges of it'.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. The abstract's explanation is stale: it was written when the old guard rule made it true, and the new measurement, already in the generated macros, contradicts it.

- **The sentence predates the new numbers.** `git blame` shows thesis.tex:90-92 ("because the extractor does not evaluate the guards almost every such transition passes") came from 296f4bdb. At that commit generated-guard-only.tex held GuardOnlyMust=369, GuardOnlyGuarded=360, GuardOnlyUnguarded=9, with CensusMust=9. So 360 of 369 guard-free edges ran a guard, and the clause was accurate then.
- **3ebbf35 changed the numbers but left the clause.** Under the router-semantics guard rule, generated-guard-only.tex now gives GuardOnlyMust=191, GuardOnlyUnguarded=150, GuardOnlyGuarded=41 and GuardOnlySites=66. generated-census.tex gives CensusMust=150 and CensusMustSites=25.
- **Most of these edges run no guard.** Only 41 of the 191 edges that pass every non-guard rule run a guard. results-must/guard-only.json shows guarded=0 in realworld and mifos and 3 of 128 in k8sdash; before this commit k8sdash had 130 guarded. Taking every guard to pass adds 41 constructs (25 to 66). The abstract's "almost every such transition passes" a guard is false on its own figures. Removing the guard rule is the only counterfactual the thesis measures, and it does not move the scarcity.
- **The commit removed a twin of this claim but missed this one.** The same commit deleted the matching sentence at the abstract's end ("the transitions a static reader cannot certify are, for the most part, behind guards it does not evaluate") but did not touch lines 90-92. The built text (thesis.txt:54) still prints the clause.
- **ch7.** ch7-conclusion.tex:25-26 (also from 296f4bdb) says "which is little, rather than what the applications do". With guards passing, the tier moves only from \CensusMust{} to \GuardOnlyMust{} edges and from \CensusMustSites{} to \GuardOnlySites{} constructs. The figure printed next to it does not support "rather than what the applications do".
- **ch5.** ch5-results.tex:1104-1105 ("where an application puts its guard decides how much of its navigation that is") is weaker but still overstated. Guard placement accounts for 41 edges in total, 29 of them ghostfolio's.

I rate it major rather than critical: the error is one stale causal clause plus two echoes, and the measured results are untouched. It is still a false statement in the abstract that the thesis's own macros contradict.
verdict.checkedEvidence:
- **Current macros:** thesis/generated-guard-only.tex (GuardOnlyMust 191, Unguarded 150, Guarded 41, Sites 66, GuardedGhostfolio 29, GuardedKdash 3, GuardedRealworld 0, GuardedMifos 0); generated-census.tex:26,34 (CensusMust 150, CensusMustSites 25); generated-round2.tex:61 (RoundTwoInScope 1777).
- **Per-app results:** route-oracle/results-must/guard-only.json (k8sdash must 128 / guarded 3; realworld and mifos guarded 0).
- **Old macros:** git show 296f4bdb:thesis-handoff/thesis/generated-guard-only.tex (369 / 360 guarded / 9 unguarded, CensusMust 9).
- **Blame:** git blame thesis.tex:90-92 and ch7-conclusion.tex:25-27 point to 296f4bdb; ch5-results.tex:1104-1105 points to 3ebbf35.
- **Commit diff:** git show 3ebbf35 -- thesis.tex shows the end-of-abstract guard sentence was removed and lines 90-92 were not touched.
- **Built PDF:** thesis.txt:54 and :5038 still print both sentences.
verdict.betterFix:
1. thesis.tex:90-92, replace ", because the extractor does not evaluate the guards almost every such transition passes;" with ": \CensusMustSites{} constructs behind \CensusMust{} edges, and taking every guard to let the navigation through raises that only to \GuardOnlySites{} constructs behind \GuardOnlyMust{} edges;".

2. ch7-conclusion.tex:24-27, replace "That measures what the extractor can prove without evaluating guards, which is little, rather than what the applications do: with every guard taken to let the navigation through, the tier would hold \GuardOnlyMust{} edges." with "Evaluating guards would add little to it: with every guard taken to let the navigation through, the tier would hold \GuardOnlyMust{} edges on \GuardOnlySites{} constructs, of which only \GuardOnlyGuarded{} edges run a guard."

3. ch5-results.tex:1104-1105, replace "and where an application puts its guard decides how much of its navigation that is." with "and where an application puts its guard moves \GuardOnlyGuarded{} edges of it, \GuardOnlyGuardedGhostfolio{} of them ghostfolio's."

Do not add a share of \RoundTwoInScope{}. There is no macro showing that the census site count and the round-two in-scope count are measured over the same universe of constructs.

title: The width table measures the class-level join the call graph replaced, not the computed attribution
where: generated-baseline.tex (whole file); used at ch1-introduction.tex:199-201, ch5-results.tex:455-462, ch5-results.tex:603-604, ch6-discussion.tex:215-218
evidence: TabScopeBaseline gives realworld 39 sites and 192 attributed pairs. That is exactly GT 'class' (183 correct + GTClassExcess=9). The call-graph level is TabAblation full realworld 39/183 and GTFullExcess=0. The pair column sums to 51807 and the site column to 1712, which match AblationClassPairs=51806 and AblationClassSites=1711, not AblationFullPairs=52210 or AblationFullSites=1717. git log shows generated-baseline.tex was last written at 7d109c7, before 22dd294 ('attribute a service navigation through a member-level call graph'). The file carries no extractor stamp. With full pairs, mifos is 791945/43113 = 18.4, not BaselineFactorMax=18.5. Realworld's mean scope is 183/39 = 4.7, not BaselineMeanScopeMin=4.9.
consequence: The third RQ3 qualification and the ch1 and ch6 width statements are measured on the rule the thesis says it discarded. They are presented as 'the computed attribution'.
fix: Re-run scope-baseline.mts on the 0027017 corpus graphs, with a provenance stamp, and regenerate \BaselineFactorMin/Max, \BaselineMeanScopeMin/Max and \BaselineBluntest*. Alternatively, compute the table from the ablation 'full' rows.

verdict.reasoning:
Refutation failed: the finding holds. scope-baseline.mts reads whatever graph the extractor last emitted to each corpus uigraph.db. Its output, generated-baseline.tex, was last committed at 7d109c7, which is before 22dd294 (the call graph) and every extractor change after it. The file has no extractorStamp line. remeasure.sh (route-oracle/remeasure.sh:55-57) regenerates ablation and ground truth but never runs scope-baseline.mts, so the 0027017 re-measure never touched this table.

scope-ablation.mjs pairsOf (lines 67-90) computes the same quantity as scope-baseline.mts: same screen filter, same scopeMembers expansion, same file:line site key. Its `full` level is read straight from the published on-disk graph (lines 112-115). The two tables therefore claim the same quantity, but they disagree in four of six rows. Comparing the baseline rows with ~/personal/uigraph-work/ablation/ablation.json:
- realworld: baseline 39/192 equals class 39/192; full is 39/183. The 9 extra pairs are exactly \GTClassExcess.
- k8sdash: baseline 62/2451 equals class; full is 62/2450.
- bitwarden: baseline 106/2110 equals class; full is 108/2284.
- mifos: baseline 1309/42874 is within one of class (1308/42873, drift from later commits); full is 1312/43113.

So Table tab:scopebaseline, captioned "The computed attribution" (ch5-results.tex:447), is the class-join extractor that the thesis says it replaced (ch5:512-514, ch5:597-598). It visibly contradicts Table tab:ablation in the same section. Its realworld row also asserts the 9 excess pairs that ch5:597 and ch1:194-198 say the analysis no longer asserts.

Recomputed from the 0027017 `full` rows (trivial = sites x screens):
- realworld: 183/39 = 4.69, factor 390/183 = 2.13.
- k8sdash: 2450/62 = 39.5 of 67 screens (59%), factor 4154/2450 = 1.70.
- bitwarden: 2284/108 = 21.15, factor 10584/2284 = 4.63.
- mifos: 43113/1312 = 32.86, factor 793760/43113 = 18.41.

Stale macros that change: \BaselineFactorMax 18.5 -> 18.4, \BaselineMeanScopeMin 4.9 -> 4.7, \BaselineSharpestAttributed 42874 -> 43113, \BaselineSharpestTrivial 791945 -> 793760, plus four table rows. The finding's 791945 for mifos keeps the old site count; the correct trivial count is 1312x605 = 793760, though the factor still rounds to 18.4. \BaselineFactorMin (1.7), \BaselineBluntest* (k8sdash, 39.5, 67, 59%) and \BaselineMeanScopeMax (39.5) are unchanged, so the qualitative RQ3 qualification survives. The defect is provenance and an internal contradiction, not a reversed conclusion.

Small overstatement in the finding: the baseline column sums (1712/51807) are within one of AblationClassSites/AblationClassPairs (1711/51806), not equal, because of mifos drift. The per-app exact matches (realworld, k8sdash, bitwarden) carry the claim.

Rated major rather than minor because the thesis rests on generated, final-extractor figures, and the table contradicts its neighbour on the one application with ground truth.
verdict.checkedEvidence:
- thesis/generated-baseline.tex: no extractor stamp. Rows: realworld 39/192, k8sdash 62/2451, bitwarden 106/2110, mifos 1309/42874. Macros: FactorMax 18.5, MeanScopeMin 4.9.
- `git log -- generated-baseline.tex` shows only 7d109c7. `git log 7d109c7..HEAD` lists 22dd294 (call graph), be43840, a8c7480 and 0027017 after it.
- thesis/generated-ablation.tex is stamped "Extractor 0027017". Its full row: realworld 39/183, k8sdash 62/2450, bitwarden 108/2284, mifos 1312/43113. AblationClassSites 1711, AblationClassPairs 51806.
- ~/personal/uigraph-work/ablation/ablation.json, class level: realworld 39/192, k8sdash 62/2451, bitwarden 106/2110, mifos 1308/42873.
- thesis/generated-groundtruth.tex: GTFullExcess 0, GTClassExcess 9, class correct 183.
- route-oracle/scope-ablation.mjs:67-90 (pairsOf) is the same metric as scope-baseline.mts. scope-ablation.mjs:112-115 reads `full` from the published db.
- route-oracle/remeasure.sh:55-57 runs scope-ablation and score-ground-truth but not scope-baseline.mts.
- Corpus dbs dated Nov 1 under ~/personal/uigraph-work/corpus/<slug>/<sub>/uigraph.db.
- Prose consuming the stale macros: ch1-introduction.tex:199-201; ch5-results.tex:447 (caption), 455-462, 579, 603-604; ch6-discussion.tex:215-218.
verdict.betterFix:
No prose change is needed: every sentence already uses \Baseline* macros, and the RQ3 wording ("at the low end names most of an application", k8sdash, "about two screens in five") stays true after regeneration. Fix the generator and its provenance:

(1) Add `extractorStamp()` from ./provenance.mjs to the header that scope-baseline.mts writes. Then add this line to route-oracle/remeasure.sh beside line 55, so it is re-measured with everything else:
pnpm -s exec tsx scope-baseline.mts "$W"/corpus/realworld/uigraph.db "$W"/corpus/alfresco/projects/aca-content/uigraph.db "$W"/corpus/ghostfolio/apps/client/uigraph.db "$W"/corpus/k8sdash/modules/web/uigraph.db "$W"/corpus/bitwarden/apps/web/uigraph.db "$W"/corpus/mifos/uigraph.db --tex > "$TEX/generated-baseline.tex"

(2) Simpler, and better: drop the second implementation. scope-ablation.mjs already measures the identical (site, screen) set as `measured.full`, along with the screen count. Have it emit \TabScopeBaseline and the \Baseline* macros from those `full` rows, under its existing 0027017 stamp. Then delete scope-baseline.mts. The width table and the full column of tab:ablation can then never disagree again.

Expected regenerated values (derived from ablation.json; read them from the regenerated file, never type them):
- \BaselineFactorMax 18.4
- \BaselineMeanScopeMin 4.7
- \BaselineSharpestAttributed 43113
- \BaselineSharpestTrivial 793760
- \BaselineFactorMin, \BaselineBluntest*, \BaselineMeanScopeMax unchanged.

title: 'All but MustFateKept' ignores the joined edge, which is still must
evidence: The fate counts are MustFateKept=2, MustFateJoined=1, MustFateGuard=10, MustFateSelfLoop=1 and MustFateCondition=6. must-context.mjs defines 'joined' as an edge that 'is must through another construct'. ch5-results.tex:1069-1071 says the joined edge 'stays must'. The abstract nevertheless says all but \MustFateKept{} 'run only once something has happened, behind a guard, or to the screen already displayed', and ch7 says 'The others ... stopped claiming to be deterministic'. In the current realworld graph, 7 of the round's 9 realworld (source, target) pairs are must: /tag/:tag, /login, /register, /editor, /editor/:slug, /article/:slug and /profile/:username/favorites, each to '/'.
consequence: The amount of the round's tier that survives is understated: 3 of 20 edges survive by the ledger, not 2. A reader cannot reconcile 'keeps 2' with ch5's 'joined ... stays must'.
fix: State it as '\MustFateKept{} keep a construct that earns must and \MustFateJoined{} stays must through another construct; the other \the\numexpr\MustCtxEdges-\MustFateKept-\MustFateJoined\relax{} run under a condition, behind a guard, or to the screen already displayed'. Better still, emit a \MustFateSurvived macro.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Three of the four cited places are wrong. The abstract's first sentence holds up.

The ledger (route-oracle/results-must/must-context.json, produced by must-context.mjs:132-138) puts each of the 20 round edges in one fate. The joined edge is realworld '/profile/:username/favorites -> /' (click:routerLink). The fate is decided in this order: kept, then joined, then guard, then self-loop, then condition (must-context.mjs:132-138). 'Joined' means that none of the edge's own constructs earns must, yet the edge is must through another construct (must-context.mjs:14-15). So this edge survives as must. I checked the current graph (uigraph-corpus/realworld/uigraph.db), and '/profile/:username/favorites -> /' click:routerLink is must there.

ch5-results.tex:1069-1071 states the same thing: '\MustFateJoined{} is joined ... the edge stays must'. Three must edges of the round's 20 therefore survive (kept 2 + joined 1), not 2. The following text is wrong as a result:

- thesis.tex:161-164 says 'all but \MustFateKept{} run only once something has happened, behind a guard, or to the screen already displayed'. The joined edge is still reachable without any condition, through the logo link.
- ch5-results.tex:943-944 and the table caption at 948 say the fourth correction 'keeps \MustFateKept{} of the tier's edges'. It keeps 3 edges must.
- ch7-conclusion.tex:138-140 says 'The others ... stopped claiming to be deterministic'. The joined edge did not stop; it is still must.

Where the finding overreaches:

1. thesis.tex:114-117 is literally accurate. The joined edge's only cited construct (article-list.component.ts:36) is classified as 'control-flow block', so it does run under a condition. 'Keeps a construct that earns must in \MustFateKept{}' is also true, because the joined edge keeps no construct it cited.
2. The 7-of-9 pair argument is mostly not evidence of an error. For 5 of those pairs (/login, /register, /editor, /editor/:slug, /article/:slug) the round's edge was a 'navigate' edge, and that edge is still may in the current graph. The must edge between those screens now is a different click:routerLink logo edge, so filing them as 'condition' is correct.

Why minor rather than major: the error is off by one edge out of 20, it understates rather than overstates, and ch5 itself reports the joined edge, so no conclusion changes. It is still a figure in the abstract and conclusion that contradicts the body.

Side note, not part of this finding: ch5:1062-1066 presents guard 10 + self-loop 1 + condition 6 as dividing up the \MustCtxAllConditional{}=17 edges. In fact the self-loop edge has an unconditional site and the joined edge has none; the totals only happen to match. Do not use \MustCtxAllConditional as the 'others' count in the fix.
verdict.checkedEvidence:
- generated-must.tex:11-16 gives MustFateKept=2, Joined=1, Guard=10, SelfLoop=1, Condition=6, Retargeted=0. generated-round2.tex:74 gives RoundTwoMustEdges=20.
- must-context.mjs:10-21 holds the fate definitions ('joined ... the same edge is must through another construct') and must-context.mjs:132-138 the order they are tested in.
- results-must/must-context.json has the per-edge rows. The joined edge is realworld '/profile/:username/favorites -> /' click:routerLink, with sites 1 and unconditionalSites 0. Its construct article-list.component.ts:36 has the condition 'control-flow block'.
- The current graph, /Users/kanetran29/personal/uigraph-corpus/realworld/uigraph.db (the --after input per remeasure.sh:45), shows '/profile/:username/favorites -> /' click:routerLink as must. For /login, /register, /editor, /editor/:slug and /article/:slug, the 'navigate' edge into / is may and a separate click:routerLink edge is must. The graph holds 9 must edges in total.
- ch5-results.tex:1069-1071 says 'the edge stays must'. ch5-results.tex:943-944 and 948 say 'keeps \MustFateKept{} of the tier's edges'. thesis.tex:161-164 says 'all but \MustFateKept{} run only once...'. ch7-conclusion.tex:138-140 says 'The others ... stopped claiming to be deterministic'.
- The built PDF text (thesis.txt lines 126, 3642, 3672, 5154) shows these lines rendered with the number 2.
- No \numexpr appears anywhere in the thesis sources.
verdict.betterFix:
The fix uses only existing macros and needs no \numexpr. Do not use \MustCtxAllConditional for the 'others' count, because that count is a different set of edges.

thesis.tex:161-164, replace from 'of its must edges, which led ...' through '... to the screen already displayed.' with: "of its \RoundTwoMustEdges{} must edges, which led to the application root and the sign-in screen, \MustFateKept{} keep a construct that earns must and \MustFateJoined{} stays must only through a construct it did not cite; of the rest, \MustFateCondition{} run only once something has happened, \MustFateGuard{} sit behind a guard, and \MustFateSelfLoop{} leads to the screen already displayed."

ch5-results.tex:943-944: "A fourth correction, made after the table was measured, finds a construct that earns must on only \MustFateKept{} of the tier's edges and keeps \MustFateJoined{} more must only through a construct it did not cite, and is reported after the first three."

ch5-results.tex:948 (caption): "... before the fourth correction of this section, which leaves \MustFateKept{} of the tier's edges must on a construct they cite and \MustFateJoined{} more on one they do not."

ch7-conclusion.tex:138-140: "... kept a construct that earns must in only \MustFateKept{} of them, and \MustFateJoined{} more stayed must only because a construct it had not cited yields it (Section~\ref{sec:res-round2}). The others did not become correct targets; they stopped claiming to be deterministic, which they had no evidence for."

thesis.tex:114-117 can stay as written.

If a single figure is wanted instead of the fate counts, add a \MustFateSurvived macro (kept+joined) to must-context.mjs's tex output rather than doing the sum in LaTeX.

title: An application whose screens all sit behind a guard is said to gain almost no must edges; k8sdash gains 125
evidence: The text reads: 'An application whose screens all sit behind a guard can gain a great deal of navigation and almost no deterministic navigation'. In results-must/tier-reading.json, k8sdash's chrome is the '' route carrying AuthGuard over every screen. CensusBaseMustKdash=0 and CensusMustKdash=125, so with attribution it gains 125 must edges, 83% of CensusMust=150. ch5-results.tex:1077-1078 itself says the guarded-parent case 'is where most of the tier now is'.
consequence: The sentence predates the router-guard rule and now contradicts the paragraph above it and the census.
fix: Delete the sentence, or replace it with: 'An application that names its guard on each route, as ghostfolio does (\GuardOnlyGuardedGhostfolio{} guarded edges), can gain a great deal of navigation and no deterministic navigation; one that guards a shared parent, as k8sdash does, gains \CensusMustKdash{} must edges.'

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds, but I'd downgrade it from major to minor.

ch5-results.tex:252-253 still says: "An application whose screens all sit behind a guard can gain a great deal of navigation and almost no deterministic navigation". Commit 3ebbf35 left this sentence unchanged, even though it rewrote the sentence just before it (lines 249-251). That earlier sentence now says k8sdash's toolbar logo link and Create button take it "from none to \CensusMustKdash{}". The census confirms this: CensusBaseMustKdash=0 and CensusMustKdash=125, which is 125 of CensusMust=150. tier-reading.json (k8sdash entry for src/chrome/template.html:30) shows k8sdash's screens all sit behind a guard. The chrome component belongs to the '' route, which carries AuthGuard and is the parent of every screen drawn. So an application whose screens are all behind a guard gains most of the tier, the opposite of what the sentence implies. mifos and bitwarden also keep their must edges behind a shared parent guard (the withShell AuthenticationGuard, and authGuard). ch5-results.tex:1076-1078 says this directly: reading guards as the router runs them lets through navigation between screens that share a guarded parent, "and that is where most of the tier now is". ch5:1101-1104 adds that where an application puts its guard decides the outcome, not whether it has one.

Why minor rather than major: the sentence says "can", and ghostfolio does fit it. Ghostfolio's may edges go from 60 to 262 with attribution (generated-census-base.tex:13 vs generated-census.tex:13), and CensusMustGhostfolio=0. So the sentence is not literally false and no number is wrong. What's wrong is the condition it names (screens behind a guard). That condition is not what decides the outcome, and the sentence right before it shows the opposite case.

On the finding's own fix: it uses \GuardOnlyGuardedGhostfolio{}, which comes from the guard-only re-extraction where every guard is taken to let the navigation through (generated-guard-only.tex; first explained at ch5:1096-1103). A parenthetical "29 guarded edges" in Section 5.x has not been defined yet at that point and measures a different instrument. Use census macros instead.
verdict.checkedEvidence: ch5-results.tex:249-253 (lines 249-251 changed in 3ebbf35; line 252, "all sit behind a guard", is unchanged context in the diff); ch5-results.tex:1074-1078, 1094-1104; generated-census.tex:13 (ghostfolio row: 0 must, 262 may), :26 CensusMust=150, :42 CensusMustGhostfolio=0, :44 CensusMustKdash=125, :46 Bitwarden=1, :48 Mifos=15; generated-census-base.tex:13 (ghostfolio: 0 must, 60 may), :44 CensusBaseMustKdash=0, :46 Bitwarden=1, :48 Mifos=15; generated-guard-only.tex:11 GuardOnlyGuardedGhostfolio=29 (guard-only run, not the census); route-oracle/results-must/tier-reading.json: k8sdash src/chrome/template.html:30 reading ('' route carries AuthGuard over every child screen); bitwarden entry (shared '' parent with authGuard); mifos entries (shared withShell AuthenticationGuard); the built PDF text (scratchpad/thesis.txt) contains the sentence once. ASSUMPTION, not checked: whether every ghostfolio screen is guarded.
verdict.betterFix: Replace ch5-results.tex:252-253 with: "Where an application puts its guard decides how much of that navigation becomes deterministic. k8sdash guards one parent of every screen, which a navigation between two of its children does not run again, and goes from \CensusBaseMustKdash{} must edges to \CensusMustKdash{}. ghostfolio names its guard on each route and holds \CensusMustGhostfolio{} must edges after attribution, however much navigation attribution adds; Section~\ref{sec:res-round2} returns to why." This uses only existing census macros and keeps the pointer to the later section. It drops the finding's \GuardOnlyGuardedGhostfolio{} parenthetical, which counts edges in the guard-only re-extraction rather than the census.

title: The prose says the corrections shrank the must tier; the current tier is larger
evidence: ch5:1114 says 'Each correction removed a claim the extractor could not support.' ch5:1129-1130 says the must tier 'was a small slice of the graph and is a smaller one now'. Round: RoundTwoMustEdges=20 of RoundTwoEdges=11601 (0.17%). Now: CensusMust=150 of CensusEdges=11901 (1.26%). k8sdash went from n/a (TabRoundTwoSoundness) to CensusMustKdash=125, and mifos from RoundTwoMustEdgesMifos=1 to CensusMustMifos=15. ch5:1077 itself says 'It is not the round's tier made smaller.'
consequence: Two stale sentences invert the direction of the fourth correction's effect on the tier.
fix: ch5:1114: 'The first three corrections and the condition rules removed claims the extractor could not support; reading guards as the router runs them added \the\numexpr\CensusMust-\RoundTwoMustEdges\relax{} edges.' ch5:1130: replace 'and is a smaller one now' with 'and is still small, \CensusMust{} of \CensusEdges{}'.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds for ch5:1129-1130. It holds only partly for ch5:1114, and its proposed fix for 1114 gives the wrong cause for the change.

1. ch5:1129-1130 contradicts the thesis itself. The sentence says the must tier "was a small slice of the graph and is a smaller one now". The thesis measures tier size in edges. At ch5:959 it writes "The tier was small --- \RoundTwoMustEdges{} edges in a graph of \RoundTwoEdges{}", and at ch5:1076 it says "It is not the round's tier made smaller." By edges the tier grew:
   - Round: RoundTwoMustEdges=20 of RoundTwoEdges=11601 (0.17%).
   - Now: CensusMust=150 of CensusEdges=11901 (1.26%).
   - Per app: k8sdash 0 to CensusMustKdash=125 ("n/a" in TabRoundTwoSoundness); mifos RoundTwoMustEdgesMifos=1 to CensusMustMifos=15.
   
   The best counter-argument does not rescue it. The paragraph counts "per cited source location", so the tier could be measured in locations instead. In that unit it went from MustCtxConstructs=36 citations to CensusMustCitedSites=31. That is a slight drop, but it does not overcome the direct contradiction with ch5:1076. The built PDF has both sentences (thesis.txt:3796 and :3851).
   
   History: the sentence came in with 296f4bd and the "Each correction" line with e76b705 ("...which empties the tier"). Both predate the router-guard rule, so the prose is out of date.

2. ch5:1114 does not invert the direction; it leaves out the additions. The sentence is about RQ1's numerator, which is counted in constructs, not edges. The round numerator works out to about 27 constructs: realworld 30.0% of 40 = 12, bitwarden 10.6% of 132 ≈ 14, mifos 0.1% of 1344 ≈ 1. That uses the TabRoundTwoSoundness percentages and the TabConversion construct counts. Now it is CensusMustSites=25, so the net change is down. Each correction also did remove claims. So "Each correction removed a claim the extractor could not support" is literally true. It hides that the fourth correction also admitted constructs: mifos about 1 to CensusMustSitesMifos=19, k8sdash 0 to CensusMustSitesKdash=2, against realworld 12 to 3 and bitwarden 14 to 1.

title: 'Only 1 of the six applications move at all'; bitwarden moves -2.3 pp in the same table

2. The macro counts gains only. compare.mjs line ~187 sets `gained: rows.filter((r) => r.convAfter > r.convBefore).length`. A fall is never counted, so "move at all" is not what the macro measures.

- accept-org-open-invite.component.ts:217

The finding holds. ch5-results.tex:889-890 says the two columns of Table tab:before-after are "ratios over the same \RoundTwoInScope{} sites". \RoundTwoInScope is 1777 (generated-round2.tex), and the PDF prints "the same 1777 sites" (thesis.txt:3609).

- realworld: 5 must out of 40 constructs = 0.125, and 12/40 = 0.300. A 39-site denominator would give 12.8% and 30.8%.
- bitwarden: 17/132 = 0.1288 and 14/132 = 0.1061.
- mifos: 2/1344 = 0.0015.

title: 'Node classes are empty', yet TabLoss and PlotLoss show node-defect losses
evidence: TabLoss has 'Node missing, other' = 40 (alf 2, gf 3, k8s 1, mif 34) and 'Constant target' = 6. I tried to refute the finding and could not. Its core holds, with one overreach.

The node classes are defined in ch4-evaluation.tex:229-239 (Table tab:loss-rules). They are the nested rules under "Owner is a route component, but that component has no node": Component unlinked, Constant path, Other, Lazy boundary and Node missing. In generated-tables.tex:44-48 (\TabLoss), Lazy boundary, Constant path and Component unlinked are all 0. The TabLoss row "Node missing, other" (the nested Other plus Node missing) is 0/2/3/1/0/34, total 40. So the node classes are not empty.

PlotLoss is the plot this caption sits on. In generated-plots.tex:27-28 it draws "Node defects" at 0.0/5.9/1.5/1.4/0.0/2.5. These shares are exactly the node-missing row over each app's construct count: 2/34, 3/198, 1/72 and 34/1344.

- fig-plots.tex:18-19, the caption: "the node classes are empty on this instrument". The rendered PDF has it at thesis.txt:2702, with the "Node defects" legend at :2687.
- ch5-results.tex:318: "the node classes are now empty (Table~\ref{tab:loss}), so there is nothing in them left to convert".
- ch5-results.tex:321: "on a corpus whose nodes are complete".

The ch5 argument therefore rests on a false premise. The real fact is stronger: \TabRecoverySource row "Out of the node classes" is 0/0/0 (generated-before-after.tex:44). So none of the 40 node-class constructs converted. The evidence did not become unmeasurable.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds. The prose claims full explanation, and the table printed directly under it has a row labelled as unexplained.

title: 41 guarded edges are counted as 41 of the 66 constructs
evidence: The text reads: 'resting on \GuardOnlySites{} (66) constructs: \GuardOnlyGuarded{} (41) of them run a guard'. In guard-only.json, 'guarded' is an edge count (0+1+29+3+8+0 = 41), and 'sites' is 3+1+32+2+9+19 = 66. The next sentence uses the same family as edges: '\GuardOnlyGuardedGhostfolio{} of the guarded edges'.
consequence: Mixing units makes 62% of the constructs look guarded. The per-construct share is not measured.
fix: '...resting on \GuardOnlySites{} constructs; \GuardOnlyGuarded{} of the \GuardOnlyMust{} edges run a guard, and for \GuardOnlySourceBehind{} of those...'

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds. Lines 1097-1099 of ch5-results.tex say "gives \GuardOnlyMust{} must edges ... resting on \GuardOnlySites{} constructs: \GuardOnlyGuarded{} of them run a guard, and for \GuardOnlySourceBehind{} of those ...". The nearest antecedent of "them" is "constructs", and the built PDF prints it that way: "resting on 66 constructs: 41 of them run a guard" (thesis.txt:3818).

The script measures something else. In route-oracle/guard-only.mjs, `guarded = must.filter((e) => e.guard)` and `sourceBehind = guarded.filter(...)` are both lists of edges. `sites` is a Set of distinct witness `file:line` locations, which are the constructs. guard-only.json confirms the sums:
- guarded edges: 0+1+29+3+8+0 = 41
- sourceBehind edges: 0+1+29+0+7+0 = 37
- sites: 3+1+32+2+9+19 = 66

No construct-level guarded count exists in the script or the JSON, so "41 of 66 constructs" is a figure nobody measured. It is also not the edge figure under another name. Ghostfolio has 32 sites but only 29 must edges, so constructs and edges do not map one to one, and the edge count cannot stand in for a construct count.

The reader is led to think about 62% of constructs (41/66) are guarded. The measured share is 41/191 edges, about 21%. The next sentence, "\GuardOnlyGuardedGhostfolio{} of the guarded edges", uses edges, so the passage switches units between two sentences.

The other uses of these macros are correct. ch7-conclusion.tex:152-153 reads "gives \GuardOnlyMust{} must edges, and for \GuardOnlySourceBehind{} of the \GuardOnlyGuarded{} that run a guard", whose antecedent is edges. ch1:180, ch7:26 and thesis.tex:122 use only \GuardOnlyMust. Only ch5 needs the fix.

I rate it major because a Results-chapter figure is reported in the wrong unit and overstates the guarded share about threefold.

- thesis-handoff/route-oracle/guard-only.mjs: `guarded = must.filter((e) => e.guard)` counts edges; `sites = new Set(...witness file:line...)` counts constructs; nothing counts guarded constructs.

title: The UrlMatcher is called the only application-side unreadable construct; the data show more
evidence: ProbeMatcherScreens=1. ProbeMissedGhostfolio=242 come from a spread of competitor records 'the extractor ... declares ... a route source it could not read' (appendix-a.tex:449-453), not from the matcher. ProbeMissedMifos=5 come from a table selected through window.env, which 'no reader of the code can say' (appendix-a.tex:454-459; ch6-discussion.tex:429-434 'decided outside the sources'). ch7:19-20 ties the 242 to 'the one application whose paths a custom matcher computes'.
consequence: RQ5's answer ('one instructive exception'; 'every other defect class resolved to a construct the extractor could read') leaves out a second application-side construct. It also misattributes 242 of 251 missed addresses to the matcher.
fix: 'two exceptions: ghostfolio's UrlMatcher (\ProbeMatcherScreens{} entry) and mifos's deployment-time table choice (\ProbeMissedMifos{} addresses); ghostfolio's \ProbeMissedGhostfolio{} missed addresses are a spread route source the extractor declares unread and does not repair.' In ch7:20, drop 'whose paths a custom matcher computes'.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds, and it understates the problem. ch5-results.tex:832-836 makes a corpus-wide claim: the UrlMatcher is "the one place in the corpus where an application expresses a route in a way static analysis cannot follow". The thesis contradicts this in two other places. First, appendix-a.tex:454-459 and ch6-discussion.tex:429-434 describe mifos's choice between two route tables. It turns on !environment.OIDC.oidcServerEnabled, which is built from window.env at deployment time, so "no reader of the code can say" which table is mounted and the selection is "decided outside the sources". Second, ch6-discussion.tex:421-427 (repeated at appendix-a.tex:510-511) describes alfresco's /about page, which a JSON manifest declares, so "no reader of the application's TypeScript can see such a route". That makes at least three routes the sources leave undecided, not one. The abstract (thesis.tex:150-152, built text line 112) and the RQ5 answer (ch7-conclusion.tex:112-116, built line 5125) both rest on the single "instructive exception".

The attribution in ch7-conclusion.tex:19-20 (built line 5033: "242 of them in the one application whose paths a custom matcher computes") is also wrong. generated-probe.tex shows ghostfolio Not minted = 242 and Matcher only = 1, with \ProbeMatcherRoutes = \ProbeMatcherScreens = 1. appendix-a.tex:448-451 and 495-499 trace the 242 to a spread of competitor records, which the extractor "declares ... a route source it could not read". It is not the matcher. Also, "whose paths a custom matcher computes" generalises one route out of ghostfolio's 377.

The spread also undercuts "With the readable classes repaired" (thesis.tex:153). It is a construct the tool could not read, it was left unrepaired, and it holds 242 of the 251 (\ProbeMissed) missed addresses.

The finding's own fix is incomplete because it names two exceptions and leaves out alfresco's manifest route. The ch5 "Every class but one" sentence can be defended if "class" means the static loss list only. Its "one place in the corpus" clause cannot.

title: mifos is said to be where the scopes are widest; its scopes are not the widest by either measure
evidence: The text says the six-hundred-screen application 'is exactly where the computed scopes are widest (Table scopebaseline)'. TabScopeBaseline: mifos mean scope 32.75 screens (5.4% of 605). BaselineBluntest=k8sdash at 39.5 screens (BaselineBluntestShare=59%). mifos is BaselineSharpest, with the narrowest relative factor of 18.5.
consequence: The future-work motivation cites a table that says the opposite.
fix: '...and that is where the most attributions are computed (\BaselineSharpestAttributed{}), though the widest scopes relative to the application are \BaselineBluntest{}'s (\BaselineBluntestShare{}).'

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds. ch6-discussion.tex:793-797 (added in 3ebbf35) says the six-hundred-screen application "is exactly where the computed scopes are widest (Table~\ref{tab:scopebaseline})". The PDF text at thesis.txt:4909-4910 renders the same sentence. Table 5.11 (\TabScopeBaseline in generated-baseline.tex) contradicts it on both measures it could mean:
(1) Absolute mean scope: mifos is 32.75 and k8sdash is 39.53. \BaselineMeanScopeMax{}=39.5 belongs to k8sdash, not mifos.
(2) Width relative to the application: mifos is 32.75/605 = 5.4%, the narrowest in the corpus. k8sdash is \BaselineBluntestShare{}=59%. Even realworld (4.92/10 = 49%) is wider than mifos.
scope-baseline.mts:96-104 sets \BaselineFactorMax{}=18.5 to mifos's factor (791945/42874) and names mifos \BaselineSharpest{}. ch5-results.tex:465-466 also calls mifos "the widest margin", meaning the narrowest attribution compared with the trivial baseline. So the future-work sentence contradicts both the table it cites and the results chapter's own reading of that table. The only defensible sense of "widest" is the total attributed pairs (42874, the largest). That counts attributions, not scope width, and the table does not support the wording. Nothing on the cited table rescues the claim.
verdict.checkedEvidence: ch6-discussion.tex:793-797 (the text). generated-baseline.tex rows: mifos 605 screens, 1309 sites, 42874 attributed pairs, mean scope 32.75, 791945 trivial pairs; k8sdash 67 screens, 2451 attributed pairs, mean scope 39.53, 4154 trivial pairs; realworld mean scope 4.92 of 10 screens. Macros: \BaselineBluntest=k8sdash, \BaselineBluntestShare=59%, \BaselineSharpest=mifos, \BaselineFactorMax=18.5, \BaselineMeanScopeMax=39.5. route-oracle/scope-baseline.mts:96-106: bluntest is the minimum factor, sharpest is the maximum factor, and MeanScopeMax is the maximum of attributed/sites. ch5-results.tex:459-468 calls mifos "the widest margin" and k8sdash the bluntest. The built PDF text (thesis.txt:4909-4910) shows the sentence as it renders. git show 3ebbf35 confirms the commit introduced the line.

Nor has it reached \BaselineBluntest{}, where the average scope is \BaselineBluntestShare{} of the application, the widest in the corpus, and where an oracle would test width most directly." It equals mifos's 42874 only because mifos is currently both the sharpest and the largest application. title: 'Far fewer on the larger applications, where node defects limit it' contradicts the recovery data
evidence: TabBeforeAfter: mifos, the largest application, recovers 0+210 of 234 = 89.7%. Realworld recovers 22/22, which ch6:66 calls 'every one', not 'nearly all'. TabCoverage gives 100.0% node coverage on all six applications, and ch5:56-57 says 'on all six applications every declared screen has a node'. The low recoveries are k8s 8/56, alfresco 4/18, bitwarden 15/53 and ghostfolio 26/72. TabRemaining attributes them mostly to 'target fully dynamic' (53) and 'not reached' (50), not to node defects.
consequence: The conclusion turns the size relation and the cause the other way round from the tables.
fix: '...recovers every attribution loss on realworld and \the\numexpr...\relax{} of mifos's, and far fewer on alfresco, k8s dashboard and bitwarden, where targets computed at run time and components no screen reaches remain (Table remaining).'

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds. I tried to refute it and could not. The sentence is ch7-conclusion.tex:105-107 (PDF text line 5118). It gets the size relation wrong and names the wrong cause.

1. **Size relation.** Size here means constructs in TabConversion. In TabBeforeAfter (generated-before-after.tex), mifos is the largest application by far, with 1344 constructs. It loses 234 to attribution and recovers 0 must + 210 may, or 89.7%. No other application except realworld (22/22) recovers more than half. The low rates are alfresco 4/18, ghostfolio 26/72, k8s 8/56 and bitwarden 15/53. Alfresco has 34 constructs against realworld's 40, so it is not larger. "Far fewer on the larger applications" is false for the largest one.

2. **"Nearly all" on realworld.** 7 + 15 = 22 of 22 is all of them, which ch6-discussion.tex already says ("recovered every one of its attribution losses").

3. **"Where node defects limit it".** I tested the strongest defence: the probe measures nodes against the screens the app actually mounts, not the 100% static coverage in TabCoverage. That defence fails.
   - The probe (generated-probe.tex TabProbe) does show nodes missing on ghostfolio (242 not minted), and TabRemaining gives ghostfolio 23 losses whose target screen has no node. So the cause fits ghostfolio.
   - k8s dashboard has 0 not minted and "Declared incomplete: no", the same node completeness as realworld. Yet it recovers only 8/56; 37 of its 48 remaining losses have a target computed at run time.
   - Alfresco's remaining losses are mostly components no screen reaches (8) and code in services or guards (6). Bitwarden's are unreached (19) and services or guards (10).
   - Across all apps, "target screen has no node" is 34 of the 170 remaining (\AttrRemaining). The other causes are run-time targets 53, unreached 50 and services or guards 31.

4. **"Realworld, where node extraction is complete".** This does not set realworld apart. TabCoverage gives 100.0% on all six applications, and the probe gives k8s the same zero-missing result.

**The suggested fix.** It uses \numexpr arithmetic on numbers typed by hand, because no per-application recovery macro exists in the generated files. It also leaves out ghostfolio and the services-or-guards cause. The better fix below uses no numbers at all and points to the generated tables.

title: Count of protocol corrections: 'Eight' against 'ten'

The finding holds. I could not refute it.

ch1-introduction.tex:173 "Four corrections" is a different set, the must-tier corrections of sec:res-round2. It is not part of this contradiction and needs no change.

title: Attribution is called the weakest-evidenced class; the defect table says otherwise
evidence: Table defects (hand-compiled): attribution has 1 method and 4 lines of evidence; guards, named outlets and constant paths have 1 method and 2. The text says all four 'are carried to two by an observation' and calls attribution 'the weakest in this respect, with one method and three observations'.
consequence: Attribution has the same method count as the other three and the most total evidence, so it is not the weakest. It is carried to four, not two.
fix: 'Four of the five accepted classes rest on one named method: guards, named outlets and constant paths are carried to two by one observation, attribution to four by three.' Drop 'weakest'.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds for ch5 and only partly for ch6. In Table tab:defects (ch5-results.tex:113-122, which the caption says is compiled by hand), attribution has Methods=1 and All=4. Its evidence is mutation plus three observations: multi-mount edge absent, manual audit, and zero-edge applications. Guards, named outlets and constant paths each have Methods=1 and All=2.

ch5-results.tex:95-96 says attribution is "the weakest in this respect, with one method and three observations". The respect named in the sentence before is resting on one named method. All four classes are tied on that, and attribution has the most evidence overall. Nothing in the table makes it weaker than, for example, guards (1 method, 1 observation). Even read as "the class that leans most on observations", having more observations on top of the same one method does not make the class weaker. So "weakest" is not supported. The same sentence lumps attribution into "carried to two by an observation", although the table shows three observations.

ch6-discussion.tex:376-378 is defensible. It says the four classes are "carried to two by an observation rather than by a second instrument", and "two" there is the two-lines admission threshold. Attribution also reaches that threshold with an observation and not with a second method, so that sentence is accurate. The finding's claim that attribution "is carried to four, not two" is therefore overstated for ch6.

No generated macro holds the defect counts (generated-plots.tex only has a "Node defects" legend entry), so the fix has to be written as words. That is consistent with the hand-compiled table.

title: Before/after plot and table disagree on mifos
where: generated-plots.tex PlotBeforeAfter (shown via ch5-results.tex:234); generated-before-after.tex TabBeforeAfter
evidence: PlotBeforeAfter draws mifos at 0.2 baseline and 0.2 with attribution. TabBeforeAfter and TabConversion give mifos 0.1% and 0.1%.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds. The figure prints 0.2 for mifos and both tables print 0.1%. The table is right and the figure is wrong, so the finding's suggested fix ("print 0.15 in both") is also wrong.

Where the numbers come from. Mifos has CONVERTED_MUST = 2 out of totalConstructs = 1344 in /Users/kanetran29/personal/uigraph-work/final7/fin/results.json, and the ctrl run has the same counts. That is 2/1344 = 0.1488%, which rounds to 0.1%. Two roundings in a row turn it into 0.2%:

2. route-oracle/to-plots.mjs makes the PlotBeforeAfter coordinates with `f1(r.conversion * 100)`, where `f1 = (x) => (Math.round(x * 10) / 10).toFixed(1)`. Math.round(1.5000000000000002) = 2, so it prints 0.2.

compare.mjs:78 (TabBeforeAfter) and to-latex.mjs:42 (TabConversion) both use `pct = (v*100).toFixed(1)`. On the same 0.0015 that gives "0.1", but only because of floating-point luck. All three generators read the same `conversion` field, so the finding's guess that the plot reads a different field is wrong. The difference comes from the two rounding functions, on top of a value that run-all.mjs already rounded once.

What the reader sees. In the built PDF the figure prints "0.2 0.2" under the mifos bars (thesis.txt:2890). TabConversion prints mifos 0.1% (thesis.txt:2629) and TabBeforeAfter prints 0.1% / 0.1% (thesis.txt:2867). These are the same comparison, on adjacent pages of ch5 (Table at ch5-results.tex:232, figure at :234). With ymax=45 the bars are visually identical, so only the printed labels disagree. title: ASSUMPTION: bitwarden is said to have the highest guard density in the corpus

So the problem is that the claim is uncited, not that it is false. Both route counts are lower bounds, so even this ratio is uncertain. title: 'Every figure on one instrument' versus mixed provenance stamps
evidence: The title page says 'Every figure is re-measured on the commit named in the generated tables', and ch6 refers to 'the instrument every figure in this thesis is measured on'. The generated files carry eb9dab80 with harness 1.8.0 (tables, before-after, plots, round2), 0027017 (census, ablation, GT, RQ4, guard-only, callgraph, expansion), dfaa8eb (must ledger), 4505fd2a (node audit) and f17a302 (earlier). generated-baseline.tex, generated-probe.tex, generated-approx.tex and generated-sweep.tex name no extractor commit.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds, and the thesis contradicts itself on this point.

1. **The title page claim is false.** thesis.tex:69-70 says "Every figure is re-measured on the commit named in the generated tables." But the generated files name at least six different commits:
   - eb9dab80: generated-tables.tex and generated-before-after.tex (lines 2-3), and generated-plots.tex
   - 0027017: generated-census.tex:2, and the ablation, callgraph, expansion, groundtruth, guard-only, must-witness and rq4 files
   - dfaa8eb: generated-must.tex:2
   - 4505fd2a: generated-node-audit.tex:2
   - f17a302: generated-earlier.tex (\EarlierCommit)
   - a8c7480: generated-sweep.tex (\SweepCommit)

   These are different instruments, not one. `git diff --stat eb9dab80 0027017 -- packages/` shows 17 extractor files changed, with 2176 insertions.

2. **The thesis says the opposite elsewhere.** The PDF text at thesis.txt:3678-3680 (from ch5) says the f17a302 figures "are read from that commit's own generated results rather than re-measured". generated-node-audit.tex is stamped "the differential test as it stood in the first round", and appendix-a.tex:16 calls those figures "as the first round measured it".

3. **The PDF never names most of these commits.** A grep of thesis.txt finds only f17a302 and a8c7480. The commits eb9dab80, 0027017, dfaa8eb and 4505fd2a appear only in LaTeX `%` comments, which do not render. So "the commit named in the generated tables" points the reader at something they cannot see.

4. **ch6 repeats the claim.** ch6-discussion.tex:24-25 says "the instrument every figure in this thesis is measured on", which is false for the same reasons.

5. **Four files name no extractor commit.**
   - generated-baseline.tex:1 and generated-approx.tex:1 record only the script that wrote them.
   - generated-probe.tex records harness 1.1.0 only.
   - generated-round2.tex records harness 1.8.0 and the date 2026-10-30 only.

title: The abstract blames unevaluated guards for the small must tier, but the guard-only run contradicts it
evidence: thesis.tex:91-92 says almost no construct is recovered as deterministic "because the extractor does not evaluate the guards almost every such transition passes". ch7:23-26 says the tier "measures what the extractor can prove without evaluating guards ... rather than what the applications do". The generated macros say otherwise. generated-guard-only.tex: \GuardOnlyMust=191 against \CensusMust=150, so only \GuardOnlyGuarded=41 edges are held back by guards. \GuardOnlySites=66 constructs against \CensusMustSites=25, out of \AblationFullSites=1717 placed sites. \GuardOnlyGuardedMifos=0 and \GuardOnlyGuardedRealworld=0. generated-must.tex: \MustCtxConditional=32 of 36 citations are demoted by conditions.
consequence: The headline causal explanation is false on the final measurement. Even if every guard passed, about 3.8% of placed sites would be must. The tier is small because of the condition rules, which mostly reflect real conditional code in the applications, not because guards are unevaluated. Readers are told the opposite in the abstract, ch1, ch5 and ch7.
fix: Replace thesis.tex:91-92 with: "...once the demotion rules the soundness property rests on are applied; most constructs run only under a condition, and taking every guard to let its navigation through would raise the tier only from \CensusMust{} to \GuardOnlyMust{} edges." Delete "so the tier measures what the extractor can prove without evaluating guards" (thesis.tex:122-123) and "rather than what the applications do" (ch7:24-25). In ch5:1103-1107, state that guards account for \GuardOnlyGuarded{} of \GuardOnlyMust{} edges and conditions for the rest.

verdict.reasoning:
The core claim holds. The guard-only run lifts only the guard rule (extract.ts:397, `gated = gate.guarded && process.env.UIGRAPH_IGNORE_GUARDS !== '1'`). Every other demotion stays in force: `common` (conditional, capMay, wildcard, unknown target, holes, aux, ambiguous), resolvers, self-loop and hidden. guard-only.mjs counts must-earning sites by the same rule as graph-census.mjs mustSiteKeys, so \GuardOnlySites=66 can be compared directly with \CensusMustSites=25. Against \AblationFullSites=1717 placed sites, lifting every guard leaves the tier at about 3.8%. That is still "almost no navigation construct". So guard non-evaluation cannot be the reason the tier is small.

thesis.tex:90-92 states the opposite as cause: "...once the demotion rules ... are applied, because the extractor does not evaluate the guards almost every such transition passes". "Almost every ... passes" a guard is also contradicted. Among edges that survive the other rules, \GuardOnlyGuarded=41 of \GuardOnlyMust=191 run a guard. Realworld and mifos run none (\GuardOnlyGuardedRealworld=0, \GuardOnlyGuardedMifos=0), and ghostfolio accounts for 29 of the 41. The thesis itself also undercuts the guard explanation: ch5:1024-1025 says each construct behind the \MustFateGuard=10 guarded bitwarden edges "also runs under a condition, so either correction alone moves them".

thesis.tex:122-123 ("so the tier measures what the extractor can prove without evaluating guards") and ch7:24-26 ("which is little, rather than what the applications do") draw the same unsupported inference. ch5:1094 frames the tier as not "a property of the applications", and ch5:1103-1104 concludes "The small tier therefore says what the extractor can prove without evaluating guards". ch7:151 repeats it.

Parts of the finding do not hold. ch1:176-180 is not an overclaim: it names conditions first ("run only once something had happened ... or behind a guard"), and it is accurate. The finding's own replacement wording ("most constructs run only under a condition") is ASSUMPTION over the whole corpus. No macro splits the 1717-to-66 drop among condition, attribution cap, unknown target, wildcard and holes. \MustCtxConditional=32 of 36 covers only the round's must-tier citations, not all sites. Severity is major rather than critical: every number printed is correct and the 191 figure is disclosed next to the claim, but the abstract's causal explanation of a headline result contradicts the thesis's own generated macros.

title: The "two blind readings" agreement (30/30) is circular and is not labelled as such
evidence: route-oracle/results-must/review-instructions.md shows four things. (a) Both readings were made by the same AI assistant, in two contexts. (b) Each reader was given the extractor's own Chapter 3 demotion-rule list as "the definition to apply". (c) review.json note: the readings "do not judge guards, route order, relative bases or self-loops", yet \MustFateGuard=10 and \MustFateSelfLoop=1 of the 20 edges were decided on exactly those grounds. (d) git log puts review.json at 296f4bd (2026-11-01 00:30), after the condition rules had been rewritten on these same constructs: b7926b7 22:26, 479cc6f 22:56, 890f830 00:05. ch5:1046 also calls the readings "each made by hand from the sources".
consequence: The 30/30 agreement only shows that the extractor implements its own rule list as the same model reads it, on the 30 constructs the rules were tuned on. It does not independently corroborate the must verdicts. "Blind" and "by hand" overstate what was done. This is the same circularity the thesis now admits for the ground truth, but here it goes unstated.
fix: Abstract: replace "Two blind readings ... agree with the extractor at 30 of the 30" with "Two readings by the AI assistant, given the extractor's condition rules and made after those rules were corrected on the same constructs, agree with its condition verdicts at ...; they do not judge guards or self-loops." In ch5:1046, replace "made by hand" with "made by the AI assistant" and add the timeline and the rule-list instruction.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the finding and could not. All four evidence points hold, and the thesis prose does not state any of them where it reports the 30/30 figure.

(a) It was the same AI in both readings. review-instructions.md says both readings were made "by the AI assistant the thesis declares, in two separate contexts". The review.json note says the same.

(b) Each reader was given the extractor's own rule list. review-instructions.md contains a paragraph headed "The definition to apply" that restates the Chapter 3 demotion rules. This includes rules first added in 890f830: ICU case, optional call, default parameter value, logical assignment, earlier break, handler defined as a bare call outside any template condition, and a component mounted only under a template condition.

(c) The agreement covers only the condition verdict.
- must-context.mjs:163 counts a reader as differing only when `runsAlways !== (c.condition === null)`. Destination, guards and self-loops are never compared.
- The review.json note says the readings "do not judge guards, route order, relative bases or self-loops".
- must-context.json fates are: guard 10, self-loop 1, condition 6, kept 2, joined 1. So \MustFateGuard=10 and \MustFateSelfLoop=1 of the \RoundTwoMustEdges=20 edges were decided on grounds the readings do not check.
- Searching every .tex file for "route order", "self-loops", "do not judge" and "condition rules" finds only one scoping phrase: ch3:186, "for the condition rules". Neither the abstract nor ch5 has any scoping.

(d) The rules were rewritten on these same constructs before the readings.
- Commit 479cc6f (2026-10-31 22:56) says the condition fixes came from "A review that classified every construct behind the published must edges by hand". 890f830 (2026-11-01 00:05) changed the rules again.
- The readings are dated 2026-11-01, and review.json first appears in 296f4bd (00:30). The rule list given to the readers already contains the 890f830 rules.

Where the overclaim is:
- Abstract, thesis.tex:117-119. It lists the fates (kept, condition, guard, self-loop) and then says "Two blind readings ... agree with the extractor at 30 of the 30". This invites the reader to take the agreement as covering the guard and self-loop verdicts. It also hides that the readers were the same model and were given the extractor's own rules. The built PDF text keeps this sentence (thesis.txt:80).
- ch5:1045-1049. It calls the review "The corroboration" and says each reading was "made by hand from the sources" (thesis.txt:3766: "each made by hand from the sources"). It never says the AI made them, that they were given the rule list, or that only conditions are compared.

Partial refutations, which lower the severity from critical to major:
- "Blind" is true in a narrow sense. The instructions forbid reading conditions.ts, nav.ts, extract.ts and results-*, so the readers never saw the extractor's verdicts. The check is therefore not literally circular. It is a spec-conformance check: it can catch places where the code does not apply its rules, but it cannot catch a wrong rule.
- ch3:184-189 does disclose that "the assistant the declaration describes" made the two readings, and limits them to "the condition rules". ch3:184-186 also concedes that the tests "share the extractor's reading of each construct, and no second classifier re-derives them".
- All the numbers are correct.

What remains wrong is the framing. The abstract and ch5 overstate independence and scope, and that unstated scope gap covers more than half the edges. This sits next to an admission that the same kind of circularity affects the ground truth.

title: The AI-use declaration leaves out the readings, gate and panels the chapters attribute to the assistant
evidence: The declaration describes only one review use: reporting disagreements, each "checked against the code before anything was changed". It also claims "the design of the analysis, the evaluation protocol ... are my own" (thesis.tex:198-200). The chapters say more. ch5:1001-1004: red-team panels were made with the assistant. ch5:1016-1018: "which the panels extended to a member no handler calls unconditionally ... an address two declared routes can answer". ch5:1026: "a panel showed" the guard rule was wrong, and the current router-guard rule came from that. The assistant's readings are also used as evaluation data: review.json supplies the 30/30 agreement. tier-reading.json (note: "read ... by the assistant") gates the census: "graph-census.mjs refuses to report a must construct that is not listed here". ch6:177-178 says the measurements were "performed by the person who wrote the tool".
consequence: The formal declaration does not cover three uses: the assistant as a measuring instrument whose agreements are reported as results; the assistant as a gate on a reported figure; and AI panels as the source of adopted analysis-design changes. It also contradicts the "design is my own" sentence. That is an academic-integrity exposure.
fix: Add to the declaration: "The assistant also (a) made the two recorded readings in results-must/review.json, whose agreement with the extractor is reported in Chapter 5; (b) wrote the per-construct readings in results-must/tier-reading.json, which the census requires before it reports a must construct; and (c) ran red-team panels whose objections led to the demotion-rule extensions and the router-guard rule of Section 5.x. I checked each adopted change against the code." Change "the design of the analysis ... are my own" to match.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds, but it is major rather than critical, because the chapters themselves name the assistant. Two passages do: ch3-analysis.tex:186-188 ("a review in which the assistant the declaration describes read the constructs ... twice and separately") and ch5-results.tex:1001-1003 ("the review and the panels were made with the assistant the declaration at the front of this thesis describes"). So nothing is concealed. The problem is that the formal declaration and three passages in the chapters contradict the result files and each other.

(1) thesis.tex:175 says "used in four ways". Lines 185-189 describe the review only as a debugging aid that reports disagreements leading to corrections. The declaration never says the assistant's readings are evaluation data. Yet results-must/review.json's note says they were "made on 2026-11-01 by the AI assistant the thesis declares, in two separate contexts". must-context.mjs:189-192 turns them into \MustReviewReaders=2, \MustReviewReadersAgree=30 and \MustReviewAgreeMin=30, and ch5:1045-1049 reports these as "The corroboration".

(2) The declaration also leaves out tier-reading.json. Its note says the file was "read ... by the assistant", and graph-census.mjs:103,121 throws if a must construct is not listed in it, so an AI-made reading gates \CensusMust=150 / \CensusMustSites=25. ch5:1085-1089 describes this reading in the passive and never says who read.

Its JSON note says the assistant made it, which the ch5 prose does not say.

verdict.reasoning: The facts check out. The conclusion drops a qualifier that ch5 gives, so the finding is real. It is minor rather than major, for three reasons. (1) ch7:149-150 is literally true: every listed construct has a reading recorded against the source. The objection is to how strong the claim sounds, not to a wrong number. (2) The same ch5 paragraph (ch5:1089-1091) already says the reading was made once, with the extractor's decisions in view, and is "not an independent second reading". So the qualifier exists in the thesis. ch7 and ch5:1116-1117 simply do not repeat it. title: The ground truth applies the analysis's own rules, not the application's real behaviour
evidence: The "method" lines of route-oracle/ground-truth/realworld.json define a site's screens three ways. (1) "screens whose routed component renders, transitively through template element selectors": the nesting relation. (2) "the shell (app.component) ... appears on every screen": the rooted/shell rule. (3) for a service, "screens from which the enclosing method can actually be called, found by searching for callers": the call-graph rule. The first version was extended with 9 sites taken from the tool's output (ch4:182-185). results-callgraph/callgraph-stats.json: realworld has bound=0 and subclass=0, so provider-binding and subclass resolution (\CGBound=5536, \CGSubclass=413 corpus-wide) are never exercised. The prose calls the ground truth "the screens each navigation site really fires from" (ch5:533, ch4:172-173), and its circularity caveat is only about timing ("written after").
consequence: \GTFullPrecision=100% and "every nested level is exactly precise" largely measure whether the code follows rules the annotator applied by hand. They do not show those rules match what the application renders. The circularity is by construction, not only by timing, and the ground truth is not exhaustive beyond the analysis's own syntactic patterns.
fix: In ch4:172-180, add: "Its method encodes the analysis's own relations (template nesting, the shell rule, and callers of a service member), so it tests whether the implementation follows those rules, not whether the rules match run-time behaviour. realworld exercises no provider binding or subclass call." Replace "really fires from" with "fires from under the rules in its method field".

verdict.reasoning:
The core of the finding holds, though two of its supporting claims are partly wrong.

1. The ground truth's rules are the analysis's own relations. The method array in route-oracle/ground-truth/realworld.json defines a site's screens in three ways:
   - template-selector containment, which is the nesting level;
   - "the shell (app.component) ... appears on every screen", which is the rooted level;
   - for a service, "callers of that method", which is the call graph.
   
   So the agreement is with the analysis's rules by construction. The ground truth is not an independent reading of what the application renders.

2. The ground truth explicitly ignores render conditions and guards. The site core/layout/header.component.html:14 (the "Sign in" link, which renders only when authState === 'unauthenticated') is recorded with screens "ALL", and its reason field says "the branch is a render condition, not a scope". The same goes for :18 (Sign up) and :27/:33/:39/:46 (the authenticated branch).
   - realworld/src/app/app.routes.ts guards /settings, /editor and /editor/:slug with requireAuth.
   - The same file guards /login and /register with !isAuth.
   - So in steady state, those branch links are recorded on screens where their branch does not render.

3. This contradicts the thesis's own definition of the true scope. ch3-analysis.tex:248-250 defines scope*(x) as "the set of screens from which x really can fire, which is a property of the application and not of any analysis", and ch3 says that is what the ground truth establishes. The prose then states the result in run-time terms:
   - "really fires from": ch1:191, ch4:173, ch5:534
   - "pairs the application really has": ch6:186, ch7:48
   - "attributes nothing the application does not": thesis.tex:134 (the abstract)
   
   \GTFullPrecision=100.0% and "none of them attributes a single pair the application does not have" (ch5:549-550) partly depend on the ground truth sharing the analysis's convention of ignoring branches and guards. The analysis attributes these header sites to ALL screens too.

Where the finding is wrong or overstated:
- It says the circularity caveat is "only about timing". That is false. ch4:179-181 already says the ground truth "is the author's reading, so it is not independent of the tool's author". What the prose never says is that the method encodes the same relations, or that conditions and guards are excluded.
- results-callgraph/callgraph-stats.json does give realworld bound=0 and subclass=0. But ch5:566-568 ("whose remaining errors would sit where this application has nothing to test them") already covers this in general terms. No macro states the per-app zero, so the proposed "realworld exercises no provider binding or subclass call" would be a hand-typed number and breaks the rule.
- Whether these pairs can "really" fire is also not clear-cut. purgeAuth after a 4XX from getCurrentUser (user.service.ts:105-110) can flip the header to unauthenticated while the user is still on a guarded screen. Even so, the ground truth does not argue reachability. It sets it by rule, so "really" is still unearned.

Severity is major because the overstated wording is in the abstract and the conclusion, and it covers the only two-direction check of the thesis's central contribution. All macro values are correct; the fix is wording only.

title: The correction narrative calls the first guard correction a fix that the final guard rule undoes
evidence: ch5:967-971 frames correction 1 as a defect: mifos's withShell AuthenticationGuard "went unread and everything below it was published as unconditional". ch5:1111 says the earlier figure "counted guarded transitions as deterministic ones", and ch5:1114 says "Each correction removed a claim the extractor could not support". The final rule (ch5:1027-1035) does not run a shared parent's canActivate again. withShell (mifos core/route/route.service.ts) is a '' level with canActivate, and \GuardOnlyGuardedMifos=0 at 0027017. Before correction 1, at f17a302, mifos held 955/981 of the earlier must edges (git show f17a302:generated-round2.tex). The condition review covered only the round's \MustCtxEdges=20 edges, not the \EarlierMustEdges=1024.
consequence: Under the thesis's final semantics, the guard that correction 1 started reading does not gate navigation inside one withShell level. So the stated reason the 1024-edge tier fell is not backed by a measurement. ch1's "Nearly every transition the earlier instruments called deterministic turned out to run only once something had happened ... or behind a guard" generalises from 20 reviewed edges to 1024.
fix: Re-run the final rules on the f17a302 must edges, or state the gap. For example, ch5:1114: "The first correction's guard reading was later narrowed by the fourth; how many of the earlier \EarlierMustEdges{} edges the final rules would keep is not measured." In ch1:176-179, limit "Nearly every transition" to "Of the \RoundTwoMustEdges{} edges the review read, all but \MustFateKept{}".

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute the finding and could not. One part is overstated: the final rule does not fully undo correction 1, it narrows it. The causal claims the finding attacks are contradicted by the thesis's own generated data.

1. **Correction 1 is framed as a fix.** At ch5:967-971 the thesis says mifos's withShell guard "went unread and everything below it was published as unconditional". ch5:964 attributes the fall from \EarlierMustEdges{}=1024 edges to \RoundTwoMustEdges{}=20 to "three corrections". At f17a302, mifos held 981 of the 1024 must edges (`git show f17a302:thesis-handoff/thesis/generated-round2.tex`, soundness row `mifos ... 955/981`). The finding's "mifos held 955/981 of the earlier must edges" misreads that row: 981 is mifos's share and 955 the clean count. The point stands.

2. **The final rule narrows that guard.** ch5:1027 says the router does not run a guard again on a level a navigation keeps. The extractor does this in `packages/adapter-angular/src/extract.ts:205`, comparing levels by `t[k].obj === s[k].obj`. The regression test at `regressions.test.ts:2258-2297` asserts it: an edge between two screens under withShell is `must` with `guard` null, and only an entry from outside, from login, is `may`. The comment in that same test, "978 of mifos's 981 must edges asserted ... transitions the running application refuses whenever that guard denies", is contradicted by its own assertion for edges inside the shell.

3. **The final measurement shows no guard holds any mifos edge off the tier.** `results-must/guard-only.json` gives mifos must 15, unguarded 15, guarded 0. That matches \CensusMustMifos{}=15 and \GuardOnlyGuardedMifos{}=0 in `generated-guard-only.tex`.

4. **Two sentences are therefore contradicted.**
   - ch5:1110-1111 says the earlier figure fell "because the earlier figure counted guarded transitions as deterministic ones". For mifos, which held 96% of that figure, the final rules attribute none of the fall to a guard.
   - ch5:1114 says "Each correction removed a claim the extractor could not support". It is contradicted for correction 1 by the point above. It is contradicted for correction 3 by ch5:1059-1060, where the weakest-modality rule "answered that question by discarding a certainty the edge had".

5. **Nothing measures what happened to each of the 1024 edges.** ch5:962-964 and `earlier-instrument.mjs` say the earlier figures are read from git and not re-measured. The construct review covered only \MustCtxEdges{}=20 edges. So ch1:176-180's "Nearly every transition the earlier instruments called deterministic turned out to run only once ... or behind a guard" rests on reading 20 edges. Only the census totals support it for the 1024: mifos 981 to 15, bitwarden 34 to 1. That is the weaker half of the finding.

6. **Where the finding overstates.** Under Angular's real semantics, each `Route.withShell` call returns a distinct object. A navigation between two feature tables therefore re-enters the shell level and runs AuthenticationGuard, so correction 1 is narrowed, not undone. The extractor compares the single AST literal at `route.service.ts:28`, so it treats every withShell level as one object and never runs that guard between mifos screens. This is a separate possible soundness gap. It does not affect the current 15 mifos must sites: per `tier-reading.json`, all are relative links within one section.

Severity is major because the results chapter's causal account of why the RQ1 tier fell is contradicted by the thesis's own macro values. The headline numbers are not affected.

title: Stale claim that applications behind a guard gain almost no must edges contradicts the new tier
evidence: ch5:252-254: "An application whose screens all sit behind a guard can gain a great deal of navigation and almost no deterministic navigation". ch4:197-199: "on an application whose screens sit behind guards ... almost every transition such an application has is conditional". Every k8sdash screen sits under ChromeComponent with canActivate:[AuthGuard] (k8sdash chrome/routing.ts), yet \CensusMustKdash=125. Every mifos screen sits under withShell's AuthenticationGuard, and \GuardOnlyGuardedMifos=0.
consequence: The prose the commit claims to have rewritten still explains results with the guard rule it replaced. That explanation is wrong for the two applications holding 140 of the 150 must edges.
fix: Delete ch5:252-254. Replace ch4:197-199 with: "...the two can be far apart: on this corpus most transitions run under a condition, so a corpus can be mostly recovered and almost nowhere deterministic."

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute it. Commit 3ebbf35 leaves both cited sentences unchanged; they appear only as diff context. Both blame the guard for an application having no deterministic navigation, which is the guard rule the commit replaced.

1. ch5-results.tex:252-253 says: "An application whose screens all sit behind a guard can gain a great deal of navigation and almost no \emph{deterministic} navigation, and Section~\ref{sec:res-round2} returns to why."
   - It follows directly after k8sdash going from none to \CensusMustKdash{}=125 must edges. Every k8sdash screen is guarded: the chrome routes carry canActivate:[AuthGuard] (modules/web/src/chrome/routing.ts) and login carries LoginGuard (index.routing.ts:20). So the application held up as the counter-case is itself an application whose screens all sit behind a guard.
   - The section the sentence points to says the opposite, at ch5:1077-1078: "Reading guards as the router runs them lets through the navigations between screens that share a guarded parent, and that is where most of the tier now is."
   - The one application the sentence does describe literally is mifos. Its edges go from 5667 to 10819 (census-base.json, census.json) and its must edges stay at \CensusBaseMustMifos{}=\CensusMustMifos{}=15. But the guard is not the reason. Every mifos screen is under withShell's AuthenticationGuard (src/app/core/route/route.service.ts). Yet with every guard let through, mifos still has 15 must edges, and \GuardOnlyGuardedMifos{}=0 of them run a guard (guard-only.json).
   - The only applications where guards do cost must edges are ghostfolio (\GuardOnlyGuardedGhostfolio{}=29) and bitwarden (8). Section res-round2 explains this by where an application places its guard (on each route, as ghostfolio does), not by whether its screens are behind one.

2. ch4-evaluation.tex:197-199 makes the same causal claim in general form: "on an application whose screens sit behind guards ... almost every transition such an application has is conditional". Under the router-guard rule, a guard on a shared parent does not demote the navigations between its children. With all guards let through, the number of must constructs stays the same for k8sdash (2) and mifos (19). The claim holds only for guards named on each route.
